name: Sukhothai
tagline: The first Thai capital, by bicycle
summary: The ruins of the 13th-century capital sit in a quiet park of ponds and trees, far calmer than Ayutthaya. Rent a bicycle, see the central zone in a morning and the outer temples at sunset.
seasonNote: March to May is very hot; the Loy Krathong festival in November fills the park with lanterns and visitors.
arrival: Fly from Bangkok to Sukhothai airport (30 km away), or take a train to Phitsanulok and a one-hour bus. Buses from Chiang Mai take 5 hours.
gettingAround: Rent a bicycle at the park gate. A blue songthaew links the old city and the new town, 12 km apart, until early evening.
cashTip: Each park zone is paid separately in cash.
foodTip: Sukhothai noodles: thin rice noodles with pork, green beans, peanuts and lime, served dry or in broth.
buyTip: Sangkhalok ceramics, made here since the 13th century.
baseArea: The old city, near the park gate, for sunrise and sunset; the new town for more restaurants

connections.note: A few flights a day; 7 hours by bus.

items.name: Wat Mahathat
items.summary: The royal temple at the heart of the old capital, with a lotus-bud chedi and rows of columns around seated Buddhas.
items.expect: The largest site in the park; little shade.
items.tip: Be at the pond on the east side at sunrise for reflections.
